verdict.rationale: Codex's own documented capabilities support a debugging loop. It can inspect code, run commands and local development tools, take an error screenshot as input, and delegate a larger investigation to subagents. It can also start work from GitHub, GitLab or Linear issues and review changes before they ship. One hands-on comment reports it fixing hard problems. However, the evidence never describes an explicit reproduce → root-cause → verify workflow, so the depth of each step is unproven. Missing for 10: documented issue-reproduction workflow, explicit root-cause/debugging guidance, documented fix verification via test runs, and stronger independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can reproduce issues, narrow down root causes, and verify fixes

citations.quote: Inspect code, make changes, run commands, and automate repeatable work without leaving your terminal.
Pass an error screenshot, architecture diagram, or design reference with the first prompt
Split up a larger investigation — subagents: Ask Codex to delegate focused work to specialized agents, then bring their findings back into the main terminal session.
Let Codex inspect files, make edits, and run the tools already installed on your machine.
Then you spin the much slower GPT 5.3-Codex and it fixes everything in 3 minutes of doing the right thing.
